summary: Converts a single multi-byte character into a wide character (one-character MB_ERR_INVALID_CHARS path of the ANSI layer). Returns 0 when the input buffer or max-byte count is null/zero. When the first byte is a NUL it writes a NUL wide char and returns 0. When no locale is set (dword_8D3F38 == 0) it assigns the byte directly as the wide char and returns 1. Otherwise it consults the character-type table (off_5E69C8) for a lead byte: single-byte characters go through MultiByteToWideChar with length 1, while lead bytes use the cbMultiByte sequence length when a3 allows it. On conversion failure it stores TLS error 42 and returns -1. Returns the number of bytes consumed on success.

local_names.v3: first byte of the input multi-byte sequence

operations.description: Return 0 when lpMultiByteStr is NULL or a3 (max bytes) is zero.
Read the first byte of the sequence: v3 = *lpMultiByteStr.
If the first byte is NUL, write 0 to the output wide char at this+0x0 (*lpWideCharStr) and return 0.
When dword_8D3F38 (locale) is zero, write v3 directly as the wide char at this+0x0 (*lpWideCharStr) and return 1 (direct byte-to-wchar assignment).
Lead-byte check: consult the character-type table off_5E69C8 indexed by v3; proceed only when the table entry is >= 0.
Call MultiByteToWideChar(CodePage, 9u, lpMultiByteStr, 1, lpWideCharStr, lpWideCharStr != 0) to convert the single character; return 1 on success.
For a lead byte take result = cbMultiByte (sequence byte count) and branch on cbMultiByte > 1.
When a3 >= cbMultiByte, call MultiByteToWideChar(CodePage, 9u, lpMultiByteStr, cbMultiByte, lpWideCharStr, lpWideCharStr != 0) to convert the full sequence; return cbMultiByte on success.
On conversion failure (or when a3 < cbMultiByte / the sequence is truncated) store error 42 via TLSOffsetGetter() and return -1.
Failure path also taken when a3 < result or when the second byte lpMultiByteStr[1] is missing from an incomplete sequence.
Return result (bytes consumed) on the successful sequence path.
Called by sub_596716 (00596716) as the single-character ANSI-to-wide conversion step.

clean_pseudocode: return MultiByteToWideChar(CodePage, 9, lpMultiByteStr, 1, lpWideCharStr, lpWideCharStr != 0) ? 1 : fail;
if (MultiByteToWideChar(CodePage, 9, lpMultiByteStr, cbMultiByte, lpWideCharStr, lpWideCharStr != 0)) return cbMultiByte;

The multi-byte/wchar argument sizes passed to MultiByteToWideChar reuse lpWideCharStr != 0 as the buffer-count argument in the raw source; whether that is decompiler artifact or intentional is unknown.
